doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Starting a new piece on the piano
summary: Asked how he would begin a commission, Lamb demonstrates starting with a bass figure and simple melody.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. If you got a commission to write a new original piece how would you start? Now let’s suppose it’s a pretty open-ended thing. It could be a solo piano composition or maybe it could turn into a group thing from there. But is there a way you approach the piano differently if you know I need to write something, I need to write something that is playable by me but other people also, as opposed to just like what you did a couple of times today already, just your hands start going.
Is there a method that you might use to get an initial idea?

You know it depends on, that’s a pretty open question but you know I think I’d probably start with some sort of you know bass, like if I was asked to compose you know something like that I might like start with
So maybe something thematic like that and then a simpler melody like if I’m thinking of somebody playing it or doubling it you know like that.
answer — I’d be thinking in simpler concepts like that, like something that somebody could really grab on to and would sound moody and lush kind of built into it right away. That’s a thought.
Thank you. I loved the second chord you played, it was like I’m not on camera but it made me go like that. It was a nice change.
